claims.summary: The first real user full-course run (Linear Algebra, 14 lessons) graded 99/A but was unshippable; the whole failure is one traced cascade (calculus-only math shard -> genome linker 0/14 -> keyword source-finder fires -> unanchored fallback providers ship off-topic readings), fixed end to end in this release.

Sixteen curated tier-1 linear-algebra concept kernels join the math shard (math-intro now 38 concepts); a linear-algebra course goes from 0/14 to 10+/14 genome-linked lessons through the real resolver, restoring judgment and grounded content.

Every open-knowledge provider searches anchored to the course subject, the token-relevance gate covers all providers (not just OpenAlex/Crossref/ERIC), OpenAlex is rate-limited with backoff so a 429 no longer swaps in ungated junk (and degraded topics are not cached), math/physics/anatomy gain discipline allowlists, and the deep grader now admits and relevance-checks encyclopedic reading lines.

Exam lessons get cumulative exams built from covered lessons' authored atoms (never connecting a topic to itself), exam-day lessons get logistics/review variants instead of teaching boilerplate, code-lab assessments get distinct rubric criteria, rubric files carry their own lesson label and exams get a Quiz-Bank handoff note instead of an empty file, and a Linear Algebra course no longer inherits a Python-programming course map.

Determiner collisions ('your the Week 4 sets'), fused sentences, a course-wide lens noun stamped into 115 sites, mid-sentence citation splices, ellipsis-truncated slide bullets, a duplicate key-terms slide, and the syllabus TOC field-code leak are all repaired at the seam.

CourseIR authoring repairs case-mismatched and dangling assessment references instead of discarding the whole response, the run digest reports the real readiness-warning count on a ready run, the compiler duration telemetry times the compile rather than the whole pipeline, and voice-pass fallbacks record their reason.
